title: Corner Compositing Spec
summary: Layer assembly recipe for Bobby. How to composite building shell, room interiors, characters, lighting, and UI into the final game view.
content:
Corner Compositing Spec

Steffen | 2026-03-16 For Bobby. The assembly recipe.

Current Approach (Working)

Bobby is using the single-image approach: full-office-warm-night.png as one background with percentage-based click target overlays. This works. The compositing spec below is for the NEXT phase when we move to dynamic room rendering (furniture placement, room customization, style pack switching).

Layer Stack (Bottom to Top)

Layer 7: UI Elements (HUD, chat, menus)           z-index: 40-50
Layer 6: Light Overlays (window glow, ambient)     z-index: 30
Layer 5: Character Sprites (agents at desks)       z-index: 20
Layer 4: Room Interiors (furniture + floor)         z-index: 10
Layer 3: Building Shell (walls, roof, CORNER sign)  z-index: 5
Layer 2: Ground Plane (dark surface, light pools)   z-index: 2
Layer 1: Void Background (dark navy gradient)       z-index: 1

Layer 1: Void Background

  • Full viewport dark navy radial gradient
  • Center: #1A1A2E (slightly lighter)
  • Edges: #0D0D1A (deep dark)
  • Subtle noise texture overlay at 1.5% opacity
  • Stars/particles optional (CSS radial-gradient dots at random positions)
  • This layer NEVER changes regardless of building state

CSS:

background: radial-gradient(ellipse at 50% 45%, #1A1A2E 0%, #12121F 40%, #0D0D1A 100%);

Layer 2: Ground Plane

  • Asset: visual-target/ground-plane.png (1024x1024)
  • Positioned below the building, centered
  • Features: dark surface with warm window light pools, building shadow, pathway
  • The ground plane extends beyond the building edges
  • Light pools correspond to room window positions and colors

Positioning: Center-aligned with the building shell. The ground plane is slightly larger than the building footprint (extends 10-15% beyond each edge).

Layer 3: Building Shell

  • Asset: visual-target/building-shell.png (transparent background)
  • The L-shaped outer structure: walls, roof edges, CORNER sign
  • Interior is transparent (cut out) so room layers show through
  • The shell provides the architectural frame
  • CORNER sign is part of this layer (glowing, always visible)

Key dimensions (in the 1024x1024 source):

  • Building spans roughly columns 100-920, rows 80-720
  • L-shape: full width at top (rows 1-3), narrow at bottom-left (rows 4-5)
  • Wall thickness: approximately 20px in source

ANIMATION: Building Breathe (Patrik Mar 16 directive) The building should NEVER feel dead. Even at idle, it breathes:

@keyframes building-breathe {
  0%, 100% { transform: translateY(0px); }
  50% { transform: translateY(-4px); }
}
.building-container {
  animation: building-breathe 6s ease-in-out infinite;
}

4px movement over 6 seconds. Subtle. The building is alive.

Layer 4: Room Interiors

Each room is a separate PNG clipped to its grid cell. These are the customizable units.

Grid Cell Positions (percentage-based, matching current overlay system):

Room Left % Top % Width % Height %
patrik 5% 28% 18% 18%
mom 18% 20% 18% 18%
alex 32% 15% 18% 18%
steve 50% 8% 18% 18%
steffen 18% 38% 18% 18%
main-hall 32% 32% 18% 18%
jacob 50% 25% 18% 18%
bobby 32% 48% 18% 18%
colton 18% 55% 18% 18%
cleo 50% 42% 18% 18%
tony 65% 28% 18% 18%
elmo 50% 55% 18% 18%
elon 65% 45% 18% 18%

Room interior rendering:

  1. Floor texture (from catalog/floors/)
  2. Wall treatment (from catalog/styles/wall-*.json)
  3. Furniture items placed per catalog/furniture/*.json position data
  4. Each room has a unique ambient color: the agent's signature color at 5-8% opacity over everything

For the current single-image approach: Room interiors are baked into full-office-warm-night.png. No separate rendering needed yet.

Layer 5: Character Sprites

  • Assets: sprites/{agent}-{state}.png (idle, thinking, speaking, done)
  • Positioned at each agent's desk within their room
  • Sprite size: 30-40% of room width for visibility
  • Characters face SE (isometric standard direction)
  • Sprite state changes based on agent status (WORKING = speaking, IDLE = idle, etc.)

Sprite rendering:

imageRendering: 'pixelated'  // preserve pixel art crispness

Layer 6: Light Overlays

These are CSS-only effects, not image assets.

  • Window light spill: box-shadow or gradient overlays from window positions
  • Agent signature glow: Colored radial gradient at low opacity per room
    • Bobby: radial-gradient(rgba(156,39,176,0.08), transparent)
    • Elon: radial-gradient(rgba(76,175,80,0.06), transparent)
    • Steffen: radial-gradient(rgba(255,183,77,0.07), transparent)
  • Active agent glow: Brighter pulse when agent status is WORKING
  • Warm ambient: Global overlay rgba(255,183,77,0.03) for warmth

Layer 7: UI Elements (BLUE HUD - Updated Mar 16)

  • HUD Strip (fixed bottom, 160px, z-index 40) -- BLUE (#0F1B2D base, #3B82F6 accent)
  • Side Menu (fixed left, 280-400px, z-index 35) -- BLUE, 20px menu items
  • Chat Input (inside HUD strip, z-index 45) -- BLUE glass, 18px text
  • Notifications (top-right toast, z-index 50) -- BLUE glass with agent-color border
  • Zoom controls (z-index 30) -- BLUE glass buttons

See projects/steffen/hud-blue-spec.md for full HUD implementation spec. All font sizes 18-20px minimum. 2px Trello borders. 48px agent portraits.

How Style Packs Work with This Stack

When switching to Crossy Road style:

  1. Layer 1 changes: background becomes bright blue sky gradient
  2. Layer 2 changes: ground plane becomes green grass with voxel trees
  3. Layer 3 changes: building shell becomes chunky voxel exterior
  4. Layer 4 changes: room interiors use Crossy Road furniture items
  5. Layer 5 changes: character sprites swap to chunky voxel versions
  6. Layer 6 changes: lighting becomes flat/bright instead of moody/warm
  7. Layer 7 stays the same: HUD adapts colors but layout is consistent

The compositing system is style-agnostic. Bobby builds it once, style packs slot in.

Transition Path

Phase 1 (Current): Single image background + overlay click targets. Working now.

Phase 2 (Next): Building shell as transparent PNG + individual room PNGs composited. Enables room customization without re-rendering the whole building.

Phase 3 (Marketplace): Dynamic furniture rendering from catalog JSON. Each room renders its furniture list at runtime. Style packs swap the asset set.

Bobby should NOT rush to Phase 2. Phase 1 works. This spec is the blueprint for when Phase 2 becomes necessary (likely when we ship the marketplace/customization features).
